title: Does grip sequence shape add to maximum strength for arthritis identification? An exploratory cross-cohort test
abstract: A primary study links handgrip asymmetry with chronic disease, while repeated-grip research documents trial-order effects. We tested two within-session shape features beyond strength and demographic summaries. A model fitted in 4346 NHANES2011–2012 adults was frozen for 4785 separately recruited2013–2014 adults. Grip sequence shape changed target weighted arthritis Brier score from 0.145452 to 0.145442, difference -0.000010, joint95% interval [-0.001045,+0.001494]. The registered incremental-prediction criterion was not met. This is exploratory same-program cross-cohort evidence for self-reported ever doctor-diagnosed arthritis, not future incidence, anatomical diagnosis or causal physiology. Independent-program validation remains incomplete.
